channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Trump, Putin and Xi at one table, without Ukraine. What Moscow wants from the proposal and why Beijing might agree.
item.description: Moscow is pushing for a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, without Kyiv or the EU. What does Russia hope to gain, and why might China be willing to take part?

item.title: [DW] Raids at far-right group's offices at European Parliament
item.description: Authorities searched the Patriots for Europe's European Parliament offices in a long-running funding inquiry. The group says the charges pertain to its predecessor and there is "no legal continuity" between the two.

item.title: [DW] Russia arrests German man, calls him a Ukraine 'mercenary'
item.description: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Nigel Farage says Reform candidates won’t be banned for backing Tommy Robinson online
item.description: Reform UK leader says far-right activist isn't his "cup of tea" but he "wouldn't ban anyone" standing for the party who has liked his posts.

item.title: [Politico Europe] BAROMÈTRE DU REJET : Le Pen, toujours moins rejetée
item.description: La nouvelle édition de l'enquête mensuelle de Cluster 17 pour POLITICO montre que Marine Le Pen est encore moins rejetée par les Français qu'au mois de septembre. Reste un mince motif d'espoir pour le bloc central.

item.title: [DW] Albania's student protests are only getting bigger
item.description: As police try to suppress anti-corruption protests by young Albanians, Prime Minister Edi Rama is claiming that "antifa" is behind the unrest. Few are buying that explanation.

item.title: [DW] Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
item.description: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
item.description: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign
item.description: Bulgaria's presidential election campaign has been shaped by recent drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea and the government's reduced support for Ukraine, making foreign policy a key factor in the first round.

item.title: [EU Observer] Peaceful demise of Vučić in Serbia stands in contrast to second weekend of riots in French cities
item.description: Vučić acknowledged defeat shortly after 9.30PM on Sunday, when exit polls put his SNS party on 105 seats in parliament, behind the reformist Student List movement, led by cardiologist Ilija Srdanović, on 135 to 140.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
item.description: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

item.title: [EU Observer] Israel’s election may disappoint everyone, as Brussels and Washington face a hard reckoning with a more ‘centrist’ leader
item.description: It’s comforting to imagine an Israeli government formed by anyone left of Benjamin Netanyahu will steer instinctively towards international expectations. But a more centrist Israeli government, like any elected government anywhere, will operate within the political space created by the policy  priorities and the empathetic capacity of its voters. There isn’t much room for Palestinians.

item.title: [DW] In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
item.description: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
item.description: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

item.title: [EU Observer] Calls mount for UN World Food Programme, which feeds over a million people in Gaza, to quit contract with Palantir
item.description: The UN food agency helping Palestinians and others in need across the world has come under scrutiny for its contract with Palantir –  the controversial US tech and AI company used by various international border police and militaries to sort data and better identify targets.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK announces further tariff suspensions on food, drink and fuel
item.description: Move is the latest "everyday fix" pushed by Chancellor John Healey ahead of the UK budget.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Frontex set for new powers to deport beyond EU borders in latest overhaul
item.description: Brussels also wants the agency to be ready to respond to border crises within 24 hours, drawing lessons from Ceuta.

item.description: Commission warns proposal risks sending cash to non-farmers

item.description: São Paulo stocks tumble after leftwing politician’s win against Flávio Bolsonaro

item.title: [Politico Europe] European defense ministers warn Putin isn’t looking for peace
item.description: The EU's top diplomat Kaja Kallas said she expects a "brutal" winter ahead for Ukraine.

item.title: [Politico Europe] French government fails to convince students to stop protests
item.description: Student groups said they will continue protesting this weekend and the weekend after.

item.title: [EU Observer] One supply scare pushed China into renewables. Two real crises still haven’t woken Europe up
item.description: The mere threat of losing control of one maritime strait turned China into a clean tech powerhouse, while Europe, hit by two real energy shocks in a few years, is wasting time watering down its green rules.

item.title: [EU Observer] One-in-three European voters now support an authoritarian or populist party, new research reveals
item.description: A historically-high number of voters have chosen parties classified as authoritarian or populist, according to a new report analysing parliamentary election results for 260 parties in 31 countries since 1946, or since the year free elections were first held.

item.title: [EU Observer] Brazil’s Lula survives Bolsonaro scare, safeguarding EU democratic ally on climate and trade
item.description: Brazil's workers' party leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defied all odds to become the first president to win the second round of elections after losing in primaries. Though his adversary has failed to acknowledge defeat, EU leaders and pro-democracy groups expressed relief at the unexpected comeback.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ex-EU commissioner Reynders faces new Belgian and Polish scrutiny after EUobserver revelations
item.description: EUobserver revealed last week that a director in the Belgian intelligence service had exchanged WhatsApp messages with ex-EU commissioner Didier Reynders, which may have been part of a criminal conspiracy to block reports into Reynders' alleged wrongdoing.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukrainian offensive creeping forward in south-east, near Velyka Novosilka (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,705)
item.description: This is where the borders of three regions meet: Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts. It has received less attention in recent months because there have been more active areas of the front.

item.title: [EU Observer] Serbia’s student protestors win parliamentary majority – setting scene for showdown with Vučić in December’s presidential poll
item.description: Serbia’s student movement has broken Aleksandar Vučić’s decade-long hold on parliament.

item.title: [EU Observer] Czech government approves first step to scrapping TV and radio licence fees in 4.36am vote, sparking protests
item.description: If changes pass, citizens will no longer pay licence fees toward Czech Television and Czech Radio, and the government will instead fund public media operations from the state budget. Opposition MPs and experts have described these far-reaching changes as a dangerous attempt to weaken public service media, threatening their independence.

item.title: [EU Observer] I led Israel’s oldest peace group and advised the Knesset. Netanyahu may fall on Tuesday, but the West Bank annexation policies won’t
item.description: Israel's election on Tuesday could bring a new government without changing the country's course. Having worked as a parliamentary adviser in the Knesset and later as executive director of Peace Now, I know how that can happen, writes Shaqued Morag.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How close is the AfD to governing in Saxony-Anhalt?
item.description: The German AfD has won two state elections in September but whether it will form local governments is not yet determined.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine blowback. How Russia is using the Global South to beat the West and strangle support for Ukraine
item.description: The Ukraine battlefield is the hottest part of Russia’s war on the West, but not the only one. The Kremlin is betting that sabotage, intimidation and other sub-threshold attacks will make Ukraine’s allies so distracted, scared and tired that they cut their support to Kyiv. Meanwhile Russia’s political warfare is reaping rewards in Africa, Asia and Latin America, writes Edward Lucas.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Exclusive] Iran war and Israeli airstrikes derail thousands of EU deportation flights
item.description: With European airlines warned off Iran, Iraq, Lebanon and low-altitude routes over Syria, Brussels’ promise to boost the return of migrants and failed asylum-seekers is colliding with hard security risks, rising costs and a backlog of 5,500 failed deportation attempts.

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: the EU’s new Canada offer, cash for farmers and Russia’s Lavrov returns to G20?
item.description: EU and Canadian leaders will look to flesh out the terms of closer cooperation on energy, trade and defence at a summit in Montréal this week.

item.title: [DW] Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
item.description: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
item.description: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
item.description: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

item.title: [DW] Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
item.description: After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.
